claim: Cellpose was retrained without pretrained weights using default parameters, except for the mean diameter which was set to 3.3.
source_text: Cellpose was retrained without pretrained weights using default parameters, except for the mean diameter which was set to 3.3 according to the provided object size estimation utility in the GUI (and visually confirmed).
evidence_reasoning: This claim describes the experimental procedure for training Cellpose.

claim: No pretrained Cellpose model was found to be suitable for the authors' data.
source_text: We investigated pretrained models provided by Cellpose, as well as attempting transfer learning, but no pretrained model was found to be suitable for our data.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on experimental observations during model evaluation.

claim: Cellpose achieved best performance with a cell probability threshold of −9 and resampling enabled after tuning.
source_text: After tuning, we found that Cellpose achieved best performance with a cell probability threshold of −9 and resampling enabled
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by hyperparameter optimization experiments.

claim: A SwinUNetR trained using WNet3D generated labels showed no significant difference from a fully supervised model across F1 vs. IoU thresholds (Kruskal-Wallis H test H=4.91, p=0.085, n=9).
source_text: To assess whether WNet3D can generalize to unseen data when trained on a specific brain volume, we trained a WNet3D from scratch using volumes cropped from a different mesoSPIM-acquired whole-brain sample, labeled with c-FOS, imaged at 561 nm with a pixel size of 5.26×5.26μm in x and y, and a step size in z of 5μm (see Additional datasets). This model was then used to generate labels for our provided dataset. A SwinUNetR model was then trained using these WNet3D generated labels, and compared to the performance of the pretrained model we provide in our napari plugin.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental results and statistical analysis.

claim: The models were evaluated using standard segmentation metrics, namely F1-Score and intersection over union (IoU).
source_text: The models were evaluated using standard segmentation metrics (Hirling et al., 2024), namely F1-Score and intersection over union (IoU).
evidence_reasoning: This claim describes standard evaluation metrics used in the field, supported by a citation.

claim: The authors used the evaluation utilities provided by StarDist.

claim: The napari plugin allows users to easily annotate data, train models, run inference, and perform various post-processing steps.
source_text: To facilitate the use of our models, we provide a napari plugin where users can easily annotate data, train models, run inference, and perform various post-processing steps.

claim: The napari plugin provides additional interfaces such as orthogonal projections to better view the ongoing labeling process.
source_text: Users may manually annotate the data in napari using our labeling interface, which provides additional interfaces such as orthogonal projections to better view the ongoing labeling process, as well as keeping track of time spent labeling each slice
evidence_reasoning: This claim describes specific features of the software tool.

claim: The authors provide a Colab Notebook to train their self-supervised model.
source_text: We additionally provide a Colab Notebook to train our self-supervised model using the same procedure described above.
evidence_reasoning: This claim describes an additional resource provided by the authors.

claim: The pretrained weights for all models are made available through the HuggingFace platform.
source_text: The pretrained weights for all our models are also made available through the HuggingFace platform (and automatically downloaded by the plugin or in Colab)
evidence_reasoning: This claim describes the availability of model weights from the study.

claim: The authors used a Kruskal-Wallis test to check the null hypothesis that the median of all models was equal.
source_text: We used Python 3.8–3.10 using the https://pypi.org/project/scikit-posthocs/ package, and we performed a Kruskal-Wallis test to check the null hypothesis that the median of all models was equal.
evidence_reasoning: This claim describes the statistical methods used in the study.

claim: When the Kruskal-Wallis test was significant, the authors used two-sided Conover-Iman post-hoc testing to test pairwise differences between models with the Holm-Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons.
source_text: When this test was significant, we used two-sided Conover-Iman post-hoc testing to test pairwise differences between models, also using the 'scikit_posthoc' implementation, with the Holm-Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons (step-down method using Bonferroni adjustments).
evidence_reasoning: This claim describes the statistical methods used in the study.
